_comment: Grafana alert rules for crok, one rule group in the llm-observability folder (Grafana provisioning API format). stack.py alerts installs it after checking that each rule's metric exists; ${prom} is the stack's Prometheus datasource uid.
title: crok-alerts

rules.title: crok: a provider is failing calls

annotations.summary: More than 10 failed model calls to {{ $labels.gen_ai_provider_name }} in 15 minutes
annotations.description: crok's retries hide these from the user, but a burst like the 22 failed OpenRouter attempts in one session on 2026-10-20 means the provider (or the route to it) is degraded. Check the Request Explorer dashboard for the error category; switching the model to the provider's direct API is the fallback.

rules.title: crok: spend today is more than twice the usual day

annotations.summary: The last 24 hours of LLM spend are {{ printf "%.1f" $values.B.Value }}x the median day of the week before
annotations.description: From the llm-history recording rules (every provider, Claude list prices and OpenRouter's bill). The median day counts at least $0.50, so a quiet week does not make every normal day an anomaly. LLM Spend History shows the split by provider and model.

rules.title: crok: MCP servers fail to start

annotations.summary: {{ humanizePercentage $values.B.Value }} of MCP server starts failed in the last 24 hours
annotations.description: 21 of 100 starts failed on one Mac in October without any signal reaching Grafana. The mcp_server workflow steps on the conversations name the server and the error type (auth, timeout, handshake).
